findings.text: Interrupts listing is exposed as sequential iteration with cached formatting widths and one-time header flag captured at position zero, descriptor traversal that yields referenced valid entries or an architecture sentinel, reference release for prior ordinary items on advance and termination, and boot registration under the interrupts name with private constraint storage.

Per-processor count rendering uses a fixed width decimal field for non-zero values and run-length accumulation for zeros, flushing accumulated zeros in bounded bulk writes built from sixteen and two hundred fifty six fold composites of a single zero field, with trailing zeros flushed after the online processor walk.

Each row after the header identifies the logical interrupt number, chooses between live per-processor counters and all-zero filler based on per-processor attributes or observed total activity, then presents chip identity with fallbacks, hardware number when a domain exists, trigger characterization when enabled, descriptor label when present, and associated handler names.

Descriptor discovery runs under read-side critical section with reference acquisition preventing reclamation after exit, row rendering holds the descriptor lock with interrupts masked while sampling chip and handler linkage, and iteration advance and termination drop the reference for ordinary descriptors while leaving the architecture sentinel unmanaged.

Interrupt behavioral attributes live as bits in a status word accessed only through helpers, including per-processor scope, balancing, trigger type, probing, request, threading, auto enable, nesting, polling, laziness, visibility, debug and reservation roles, with the reservation bit reused as proc visibility and public macro names deliberately unusable.

Local interrupt masking behaves as a nesting count where each disable needs a matching enable, repeated disables keep the masked state until the outermost enable restores availability, and flag save and restore preserve the prior masked state across nested operations, with suite setup and teardown requiring the enabled state.

Deferred interrupt replay drains a global resend queue under its dedicated lock, unlinking one descriptor at a time and invoking its dispatch operation without holding the lock before reacquiring to continue until empty.

Spurious interrupt polling runs at one tenth of a second granularity, allows only one concurrent poll through atomic entry counting, records the polling processor, skips logical zero, examines only entries flagged as spuriously disabled using a racy read, masks local interrupts around trial handling of flagged entries, and always rearms itself for the next interval.
Deferred spurious marker corresponds to the most significant bit of a thirty-two bit word.
Spurious poll period equals one tenth of the kernel tick rate.
Zero count filler uses ten character fields with sixteen and two hundred fifty six entry bulk composites for efficient sequential output.

Three boot controls govern interrupt diagnostics, namely a lockup detection disable flag, a misrouted fixup enable, and a combined fixup plus polling enable, where the latter two are rejected on fully preemptible builds and otherwise select distinct fixup modes with performance warnings.
Alarm handling is organized per timer type with each base containing a spin lock, an ordered expiry queue, callbacks to obtain current time in two representations, and an associated clock identifier.

Alarm state is partitioned by locks with per-type base locks serializing queue membership and expiry updates, a dedicated freezer lock protecting suspend snapshot values, and a device lock protecting device selection and retrieval, all acquired with interrupt state preserved.

An alarm carries an enqueued marker that makes insertion idempotent by removing any prior queue linkage before adding and makes removal a no-op when absent, starting life in the inactive state with initialized queue linkage and assigned type and callback.

Real time clock backing is chosen at most once among alarm-capable wakeup devices through a class interface, registering a wakeup platform child and retaining module and device references only on successful adoption, with no-op variants when the backing feature is unavailable.

Suspend handling snapshots and clears freezer state, scans all alarm types for the earliest queued expiry relative to each base clock, stays awake when no timer exists or when the nearest deadline is within about two seconds, otherwise programs the real time clock bounded by device limits and cancels it on resume, while builds without backing simply succeed.

Externally usable operations include retrieval of the chosen real time clock device, querying remaining time until expiry, initializing an alarm with type and callback, starting an alarm with absolute or relative deadline, initializing a high resolution timer, saturating time addition, and starting a high resolution timer with user reprogram checks.

A configured high resolution timer honors soft versus hard expiry selection with forced soft behavior on fully preemptible builds unless hard was requested, uses monotonic time for relative real time requests, binds to the current processor clock base with soft offset, preserves laziness attribute, and always ends with a usable callback.

High resolution timer base access serializes on the owning processor lock with interrupt state preserved, where the migratable variant repeatedly samples the current base and retries when migration is detected while the simple variant locks directly, and user start holds this protection across common start and conditional reprogram decisions.

Known racy or delicate points include unsynchronized sampling of total counts and spurious disabled state where staleness is tolerated, invocation of replay handlers without holding the queue lock requiring handlers to tolerate concurrent queue changes, and timer configuration that depends on current processor state and therefore must not migrate mid-initialization.
Relative deadline computation uses saturating addition that clamps overflow or negative results to the maximum representable user timeout rather than wrapping.
The interrupt proc private header defines a unique inclusion guard preventing multiple inclusion.

Expiry processing removes the alarm from its ordered queue under the base lock, invokes the registered callback with current base time when present, records a trace event, and never requests automatic restart, while remaining time is defined as expiry minus current base time.
